0.title: Truth and Grace for Broken Covenants
0.overview:
Divorce touches almost every family and church. Some readers have been divorced. Some are in painful marriages and wonder whether they may leave. Some have remarried and wonder whether they did wrong. Some are children of divorce, still feeling its effects. And many churches struggle to know how to apply Scripture with both faithfulness and compassion.

The Bible speaks clearly about God's design for marriage and his hatred of covenant-breaking. It also speaks honestly about a world where marriages are broken by sin, and it gives limited permission for divorce in certain situations. Christians have disagreed about the details, and this study sets out the main views before giving a verdict.

Above all, the gospel speaks to this subject with grace. Jesus spoke tenderly to a woman who had had five husbands (John 4). No divorce is beyond God's forgiveness, and no divorced person is a second-class Christian. The church must hold God's standard high and its arms wide open.

Five units: (1) God's Design and the Pain of Divorce; (2) Why Moses Permitted Divorce; (3) Grounds for Divorce; (4) Abuse, Separation and Hard Cases; (5) Remarriage and Grace. The Christian Marriage study covers building strong marriages.

1.title: God's Design and the Pain of Divorce
1.overview:
One flesh. Marriage was God's idea. Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh (Gen 2:24). Marriage is a covenant, a solemn promise before God, joining husband and wife in a lifelong union of body, life and love.

What God has joined. When the Pharisees asked Jesus about divorce, he went back to creation and concluded, So they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate (Matt 19:6). Marriage is not merely a human contract that can be ended when feelings change. God himself joins husband and wife.

God hates covenant-breaking. Through Malachi, God rebuked men who were abandoning their wives. The LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant (Mal 2:14). He went on: For the man who does not love his wife but divorces her, says the LORD, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence (Mal 2:16). Unjust divorce is a form of violence against a spouse.

Marriage pictures Christ and the church. Paul says marriage is a picture of Christ's covenant love for his church (Eph 5:31-32). Christ never abandons his bride. That is why faithfulness in marriage matters so much.

The pain of divorce. Divorce tears apart what God joined, and the tearing hurts. Spouses, children, extended families and churches all suffer. Even when divorce is permitted, it is always the result of sin somewhere, and always a tragedy. It should be the last resort, never the first.
1.theology:
Covenant, not contract: A contract can be ended when one party fails to deliver. A covenant is a binding promise, often made before witnesses and before God. Christian marriage vows ("till death us do part") reflect this.

Reconciliation first: Because of God's design, the first goal in a troubled marriage should always be repentance, forgiveness and reconciliation. The Forgiveness and Reconciliation study explores this.

Grace for the divorced: To say God hates divorce is not to say God hates divorced people. Many divorced people were sinned against. All, like every sinner, are welcome at the cross.
1.examples:
Then: In Malachi's day, men in Judah were divorcing their Jewish wives to marry younger foreign women. They continued to bring offerings to the temple, weeping when God did not accept them (Mal 2:13-14). God was not interested in worship from men who betrayed their wives.

Now: A couple whose marriage has grown cold are both thinking about divorce. Before deciding, they agree to see a Christian counsellor and read Matthew 19 together. It is hard work, with months of honesty and repentance. Two years later, their marriage is not perfect, but it is alive. They are glad they did not give up.

A simple test: If you are married, are you building your marriage on covenant commitment or on feelings?

verseByVerse.quote: And the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man he made into a woman and brought her to the man. Then the man said, "This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man." Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh. And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God brought the woman to the man, and he rejoiced. Then comes the definition of marriage: leaving parents, holding fast to one's spouse, becoming one flesh. Jesus quoted this verse as God's own word about marriage (Matt 19:5). Every discussion of divorce must start here.

verseByVerse.quote: And Pharisees came up to him and tested him by asking, "Is it lawful to divorce one's wife for any cause?" He answered, "Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, 'Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh'? So they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisees tried to trap Jesus with a question about divorce for any cause. Jesus did not start with exceptions. He started with God's design: male and female, one flesh, joined by God. What God has joined, no one should separate.

verseByVerse.quote: And this second thing you do. You cover the LORD's altar with tears, with weeping and groaning because he no longer regards the offering or accepts it with favor from your hand. But you say, "Why does he not?" Because the LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant. Did he not make them one, with a portion of the Spirit in their union? And what was the one God seeking? Godly offspring. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you be faithless to the wife of your youth. "For the man who does not love his wife but divorces her, says the LORD, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God refuses the offerings of men who have been faithless to the wives of their youth. He was witness to their covenant. He made them one, seeking godly offspring. Divorce without just cause covers a man's garment with violence. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless.

verseByVerse.quote: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, so that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, that she might be holy and without blemish. In the same way husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the church, because we are members of his body. "Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh." This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church. However, let each one of you love his wife as himself, and let the wife see that she respects her husband. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her. Paul quotes Genesis 2:24 and says it refers to Christ and the church. Marriage is a living picture of the gospel. Faithfulness in marriage proclaims Christ's faithfulness.

1.reflection:
Why did Jesus begin his answer on divorce with creation?

What does Malachi 2:13-16 reveal about how God sees covenant-breaking?

How does marriage picture Christ and the church?

How can churches uphold God's design without condemning the divorced?

2.title: Why Moses Permitted Divorce
2.overview:
The law of Moses. Deuteronomy 24:1-4 assumed that divorce happened in Israel and regulated it. If a man divorced his wife for some indecency, he had to give her a certificate of divorce. If she married another man and that marriage ended, the first husband could not take her back. The law did not command divorce. It limited its damage, especially to the woman, who with a certificate was free to remarry.

Because of hardness of heart. The Pharisees asked Jesus, Why then did Moses command one to give a certificate of divorce and to send her away? Jesus answered, Because of your hardness of heart Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so (Matt 19:7-8). Divorce was a concession to human sin, not part of God's original design.

The debate in Jesus' day. Jewish teachers disagreed over Deuteronomy 24. Some held that a man could divorce his wife for almost any reason. Others limited it to serious sexual sin. The Pharisees' question, Is it lawful to divorce one's wife for any cause? (Matt 19:3), was a trap set in the middle of this debate.

God's own divorce. Strikingly, God himself speaks of giving faithless Israel a decree of divorce because of her persistent adultery with idols (Jer 3:8). This shows that divorce is not always sinful for the innocent party. God was the wronged husband. Yet even then, God called Israel to return (Jer 3:12-14).

Jesus raised the standard. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said, But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery (Matt 5:32). He rejected easy divorce and restored the seriousness of the marriage covenant.
2.theology:
Permission, not command: Moses permitted divorce; he did not command it. Jesus permits divorce for sexual immorality; he does not require it. Forgiveness and reconciliation remain the better path wherever possible.

Protecting the vulnerable: In the ancient world, a woman sent away without a certificate could not remarry and might be left destitute. The certificate protected her. God's law cared for the vulnerable even when regulating sin.

Hardness of heart: The root of divorce is hardness of heart: a refusal to forgive, repent or keep promises. The gospel softens hearts, which is why Christians should be slow to divorce.
2.examples:
Then: Hosea's wife Gomer was repeatedly unfaithful. Yet God told Hosea to buy her back and love her, as the LORD loves faithless Israel (Hos 3:1-3). Hosea's marriage became a living picture of God's relentless love.

Now: A woman discovers her husband has been having an affair. She has biblical grounds for divorce. But he repents deeply, ends the affair and seeks counselling. With much pain and prayer, she chooses to forgive and rebuild. She knows she was not required to, but she believes God has helped her. It takes years, but their marriage is restored.

A simple test: Do you see divorce as a right or as a sad concession to sin?

verseByVerse.quote: "When a man takes a wife and marries her, if then she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce and puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, and she departs out of his house, and if she goes and becomes another man's wife, and the latter man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce and puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, or if the latter man dies, who took her to be his wife, then her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination before the LORD. And you shall not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you for an inheritance. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This law regulated divorce rather than commanding it. A husband who divorced his wife had to give her a written certificate, freeing her to remarry. He could not later take her back after she had married another. The law aimed to discourage hasty divorce and protect the woman.

verseByVerse.quote: They said to him, "Why then did Moses command one to give a certificate of divorce and to send her away?" He said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. And I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisees thought Moses commanded divorce. Jesus corrected them: Moses allowed it because of hard hearts, but it was not so from the beginning. Then he gave his own teaching: divorce and remarriage is adultery, except for sexual immorality.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah: "Have you seen what she did, that faithless one, Israel, how she went up on every high hill and under every green tree, and there played the whore? And I thought, 'After she has done all this she will return to me,' but she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it. She saw that for all the adulteries of that faithless one, Israel, I had sent her away with a decree of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but she too went and played the whore. Because she took her whoredom lightly, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and tree. Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense, declares the LORD." And the LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah. Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, "'Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD. I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful, declares the LORD; I will not be angry forever. Only acknowledge your guilt, that you rebelled against the LORD your God and scattered your favors among foreigners under every green tree, and that you have not obeyed my voice, declares the LORD. Return, O faithless children, declares the LORD; for I am your master; I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God describes Israel's repeated spiritual adultery. He gave her a decree of divorce, yet Judah did not learn. Still God calls, Return, faithless Israel. Even the divine husband who was wronged longs for reconciliation.

verseByVerse.quote: "It was also said, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.' But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus quotes the common understanding of the law and sharpens it. Divorce is not a casual matter. Except for sexual immorality, divorce pushes a spouse toward adultery. Jesus restores the seriousness of marriage against a culture of easy divorce.

2.reflection:
Why did Moses permit divorce, according to Jesus?

What does God's "divorce" of Israel in Jeremiah 3 teach us?

How did Jesus raise the standard of marriage above the practice of his day?

What is the difference between permitting and commanding divorce?

3.title: Grounds for Divorce
3.overview:
Does Scripture permit divorce at all? If so, when? This is where Christians differ most.

Sexual immorality. Jesus said, And I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery (Matt 19:9). Jesus' exception shows that sexual unfaithfulness so breaks the one-flesh union that the innocent spouse may end the marriage. This permission is not a requirement; the wronged spouse may forgive and stay.

Desertion by an unbeliever. Paul addresses a situation Jesus did not: a believer married to an unbeliever. If the unbeliever is willing to stay, the believer should not divorce (1 Cor 7:12-13). But if the unbelieving partner separates, let it be so. In such cases the brother or sister is not enslaved. God has called you to peace (1 Cor 7:15). When an unbelieving spouse abandons the marriage, the believer is not bound.

Separation without grounds. For believers married to believers, Paul repeats Jesus' teaching: the wife should not separate from her husband (but if she does, she should remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband), and the husband should not divorce his wife (1 Cor 7:10-11). Those who separate without biblical grounds should seek reconciliation.

What is not a ground. Incompatibility, unhappiness, falling out of love, boredom or finding someone else are not biblical grounds for divorce. These are reasons to seek help, repent and rebuild.
3.theology:
The views. Some Christians hold that divorce is never permitted, reading Mark 10:11-12 and Luke 16:18, which have no exception. Others hold that adultery is the only ground. Others, following the historic Protestant confessions, permit divorce for adultery and for wilful desertion that cannot be remedied. Some go further, allowing divorce for many reasons.

The verdict: The confessional view is the most faithful. Matthew records Jesus' exception for sexual immorality, which Mark and Luke assume rather than state. Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians 7:15 adds desertion by an unbeliever, and many Reformed churches apply this principle to a professing believer who deserts and refuses all correction, being treated as an unbeliever (Matt 18:17). Outside these grounds, believers should not divorce.

The church's role: Decisions about divorce should not be made alone. Elders and wise counsellors should be involved, to seek reconciliation, discern the situation and protect the vulnerable.
3.examples:
Then: In Corinth, some new believers wondered whether they should leave unbelieving spouses. Paul told them to stay if the spouse was willing, because the believer's presence was a blessing to the family. For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? (1 Cor 7:16).

Now: A man's wife leaves him and their children, moves in with another man and refuses all contact with the church. The elders try for many months to call her to repentance. Eventually, after she files for divorce, they counsel him that he is free. He grieves deeply, but he is not condemned.

A simple test: If someone asked you what Scripture says about grounds for divorce, could you explain Matthew 19:9 and 1 Corinthians 7:15?

verseByVerse.quote: And I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery." The disciples said to him, "If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry." But he said to them, "Not everyone can receive this saying, but only those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who have been so from birth, and there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to receive this receive it." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus' teaching is so strict that the disciples say it might be better not to marry. Jesus allows divorce only for sexual immorality, and says that remarriage after any other divorce is adultery. He then speaks of those who remain single for the kingdom. Marriage is serious; singleness is honourable.

verseByVerse.quote: To the married I give this charge (not I, but the Lord): the wife should not separate from her husband (but if she does, she should remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband), and the husband should not divorce his wife. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul passes on the Lord's own command: spouses should not separate. If a wife does separate without grounds, she should remain unmarried or be reconciled. Separation is not a loophole for remarriage. The goal is restoration.

verseByVerse.quote: To the rest I say (I, not the Lord) that if any brother has a wife who is an unbeliever, and she consents to live with him, he should not divorce her. If any woman has a husband who is an unbeliever, and he consents to live with her, she should not divorce him. For the unbelieving husband is made holy because of his wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy because of her husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy. But if the unbelieving partner separates, let it be so. In such cases the brother or sister is not enslaved. God has called you to peace. For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife? (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul addresses mixed marriages. The believer should not leave a willing unbelieving spouse; the believer's presence sanctifies the home. But if the unbeliever leaves, the believer is not enslaved. God has called us to peace. Desertion releases the deserted spouse.

verseByVerse.quote: And in the house the disciples asked him again about this matter. And he said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her, and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Privately, the disciples asked Jesus about divorce. He said that whoever divorces and remarries commits adultery, whether husband or wife. Mark does not record the exception for sexual immorality. Many explain this by noting that Mark's readers would have assumed adultery ended a marriage, as Jewish and Roman law already did.

3.reflection:
What are the two grounds for divorce taught in Scripture?

Why are incompatibility or unhappiness not biblical grounds for divorce?

How should Mark 10:11-12 and Matthew 19:9 be read together?

Why should decisions about divorce involve the church's elders?

4.title: Abuse, Separation and Hard Cases
4.overview:
Some of the most painful situations involve abuse: physical violence, sexual abuse, threats, or severe and controlling emotional cruelty. What does Scripture say to a spouse living with abuse?

Safety first. The charge that a wife should not separate (1 Cor 7:10) does not require anyone to stay where they or their children are in danger. Leaving to be safe is not the separation Paul forbids. Scripture repeatedly commends fleeing from danger: David fled from Saul, and Jesus told his followers to flee persecution (Matt 10:23). The prudent sees danger and hides himself (Prov 22:3). A church must never send a victim back to an abuser.

Abuse is a crime. Abuse is a crime as well as a sin. It should be reported to the authorities, who are God's servant for your good (Rom 13:4). The abuser should also face the church's discipline.

Does abuse end the marriage? Whether persistent, unrepentant abuse ends the marriage itself is a harder question. Many Reformed pastors and church courts treat it as a form of the desertion Paul describes in 1 Corinthians 7:15, since the abuser has abandoned every promise of the marriage while remaining under the same roof. A spouse who has been driven out by violence has been deserted.

Repentance and trust. An abuser who claims repentance must show it over time: accepting consequences, seeking help, submitting to accountability and not demanding that the victim return. Forgiveness can be given, but trust must be rebuilt slowly, and safety must come first.

Other hard cases. Some situations are complicated: addiction, mental illness, a spouse who is a Christian in name only, financial abandonment. These require wise, patient pastoral care, honest assessment and prayer. Every case is different, and each needs individual care.
4.theology:
Headship is not tyranny: Scripture calls husbands to love their wives as Christ loved the church, giving himself up for her (Eph 5:25). A husband who abuses his wife is not exercising headship; he is betraying it. Complementarian teaching must never be used to excuse abuse.

Violence and covenant-breaking: Malachi says that the man who divorces his wife without love covers his garment with violence (Mal 2:16). Violence and faithlessness are linked. Abuse breaks the covenant in its heart.

The church's responsibility: Churches must take reports of abuse seriously, protect victims, involve authorities and not prioritise keeping a marriage together over the safety of its members.
4.examples:
Then: When Saul tried repeatedly to kill David, David fled, even though Saul was the anointed king. Michal helped David escape through a window (1 Sam 19:11-12). Fleeing violence is not faithlessness.

Now: A woman finally tells her pastor that her husband has hit her for years. The pastor believes her, helps her find a safe place to stay with her children, encourages her to contact the police and confronts the husband with the elders. The church supports her practically and spiritually. When the husband refuses to repent, the elders counsel her that she is not bound.

A simple test: Does your church know how to respond to abuse? What would you do if someone confided in you?

verseByVerse.quote: The prudent sees danger and hides himself, but the simple go on and suffer for it. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The prudent person sees danger and hides; the simple go on and suffer for it. Wisdom does not ignore danger. A spouse or parent who seeks safety from violence is acting wisely, not faithlessly.

verseByVerse.quote: Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God. Therefore whoever resists the authorities resists what God has appointed, and those who resist will incur judgment. For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Would you have no fear of the one who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval, for he is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain. For he is the servant of God, an avenger who carries out God's wrath on the wrongdoer. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Government is God's servant for good, bearing the sword against wrongdoers. Reporting abuse to the authorities is not revenge or betrayal; it is using the protection God has provided. The church and the state each have a role in restraining evil.

verseByVerse.quote: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, so that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, that she might be holy and without blemish. In the same way husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the church, (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church, nourishing and cherishing them as their own bodies. Christ's headship is self-sacrificing love, never cruelty. A husband who harms his wife harms himself and betrays the gospel picture of marriage.

verseByVerse.quote: Then a harmful spirit from the LORD came upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And David was playing the lyre. And Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he eluded Saul, so that he struck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night. Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him, that he might kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him, "If you do not escape with your life tonight, tomorrow you will be killed." So Michal let David down through the window, and he fled away and escaped. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Saul, in a jealous rage, threw a spear at David. David escaped. When Saul sent men to kill him, Michal let him down through a window. David fled for his life. Scripture does not condemn him for leaving a dangerous situation.

4.reflection:
Why must safety come first in situations of abuse?

Why is it wrong to use biblical teaching on marriage to keep victims in danger?

How should a church respond to a report of abuse?

What does true repentance from an abuser look like?

5.title: Remarriage and Grace
5.overview:
May the innocent party remarry? Where a marriage has been broken by a spouse's adultery, Jesus' words in Matthew 19:9 imply that the innocent partner who remarries does not commit adultery. Where a believer has been deserted, Paul says the believer is not enslaved (1 Cor 7:15). The historic Protestant confessions conclude that remarriage is then permitted, as if the offending party were dead.

When remarriage is not permitted. Paul's instruction to remain unmarried or else be reconciled (1 Cor 7:11) is given to the one who has separated without grounds. Those who divorce without biblical grounds should seek reconciliation, not a new marriage.

Widows and widowers. Death ends a marriage. A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39).

Those already remarried. Many Christians remarried before coming to faith, or without understanding Scripture, or in situations that were not biblically clear. They are not to break up the marriage they are in. They are to repent of any sin in how it began and keep the vows they have made. A second divorce would not undo the first; it would add another broken covenant.

Grace for the divorced. Jesus met a Samaritan woman at a well who had had five husbands and was living with a man who was not her husband (John 4:17-18). He did not ignore her situation, but he offered her living water, and she became a witness to her whole town. No divorce is beyond the reach of Christ's forgiveness. Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation (2 Cor 5:17).

The church's welcome. Divorced people should be fully welcomed in the church, cared for, included and loved. Their children need special care. Single parents need practical support. The church is a family for those whose families have been broken.
5.theology:
Remarriage: the views. Some Christians hold that remarriage is never allowed while a former spouse lives, appealing to Romans 7:2-3, 1 Corinthians 7:39 and Mark 10:11-12. Others hold that the innocent party in a divorce for adultery or desertion may remarry. Some allow remarriage more broadly.

The verdict: The innocent party in a biblically justified divorce may remarry. Jesus' exception in Matthew 19:9 governs both the divorce and the remarriage that follows. Being "not enslaved" (1 Cor 7:15) means free from the marriage bond. Romans 7:2-3 and 1 Corinthians 7:39 describe the normal rule for an intact marriage, not the situation after adultery or desertion.

Church leadership: Whether a divorced or remarried man may serve as an elder is debated. The husband of one wife (1 Tim 3:2) most naturally means a man faithful to his wife. Elders must weigh the circumstances and the man's present reputation.
5.examples:
Then: Rahab, a former prostitute, and Ruth, a Moabite widow, are both named in the genealogy of Jesus (Matt 1:5). God's grace weaves broken stories into his redemption.

Now: A man divorced his first wife years ago, before he was a Christian, for no good reason. He has since remarried. After coming to faith, he is troubled by Matthew 19:9. His pastor helps him see that he should not leave his present wife, but repent before God, seek his first wife's forgiveness if possible, and be faithful to the marriage he is in. He finds peace.

A simple test: How does your church treat divorced and remarried people? Is it a place of both truth and grace?

verseByVerse.quote: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord. Yet in my judgment she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. If he dies, she is free to marry whom she wishes, only in the Lord. Paul thinks she may be happier remaining single, but marriage is permitted. Death ends the marriage bond, and a believer must marry a believer.

verseByVerse.quote: The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty or have to come here to draw water." Jesus said to her, "Go, call your husband, and come here." The woman answered him, "I have no husband." Jesus said to her, "You are right in saying, 'I have no husband'; for you have had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband. What you have said is true." The woman said to him, "Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Samaritan woman asked for living water. Jesus told her to call her husband. She said she had none, and Jesus revealed that she had had five, and the man she now had was not her husband. He did not shame her; he revealed himself as the Messiah. Truth spoken in grace led to her salvation.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come. All this is from God, who through Christ reconciled us to himself and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation. Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ, God making his appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God. For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: In Christ, a person is a new creation. The old has passed away. God does not count trespasses against those reconciled to him. This truth reaches the divorced and remarried as fully as anyone. The past does not define those who are in Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: Or do you not know, brothers —for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law is binding on a person only as long as he lives? For a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives, but if her husband dies she is released from the law of marriage. Accordingly, she will be called an adulteress if she lives with another man while her husband is alive. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, and if she marries another man she is not an adulteress. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul uses marriage as an illustration of the believer's freedom from the law. A wife is bound to her husband while he lives; if he dies, she is free. Paul is illustrating, not giving a full treatment of divorce. But the illustration shows how seriously he takes the marriage bond.
